With the advent of powerful computer-aided engineering tools these structures can be accurately modelled and fully characterized before any metal is cut thus resulting in substantial savings in time and money.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of a terrestrial DAB single frequency network for Nordrhein-Westfalen
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In cooperation with the Westdeutscher Rundfunk a DAB single frequency network operating in TV Channel 12 was planned for the coverage of Nordrhein-Westfalen. Field-strength calculations were carried out using the terrain information from a digital topographical data base. Not only waves propagating directly from the transmitter to the receiver were taken into account, but also different kinds of reflected waves in the real three-dimensional terrain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a power divider network for a slotted waveguide array using finite element and finite difference techniques
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The most critical component in the power divider network for planar broadwall slotted waveguide arrays is the reactive T splitter 3-port. It has to be designed precisely for various split ratios in order that the power divider network produces the amplitude weighting required for the array distribution function. Since the feed network cannot tolerate an impedance mismatch, the VSWR at the central port of the T junction has to be kept very low. Also, in the mechanical layout of the antenna the effective path length differences between the T splitter output ports has to be taken into account in order to realize equal path length (constant phase) array excitation. The analysis of the T splitter is presented using field theoretical methods and measurement results. It will be shown that the T splitter results can also be combined with measured characteristics of straight and bent waveguides in simulation of the full power divider network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stacked rectangular ring antenna for GPS mobile receiver
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A microstrip patch antenna array for use with the GPS receiver has been developed. The paper presents microstrip stacked rectangular-ring patches with low cross polarisation over an extremely wide beamwidth (close to hemisphere). The desegmentation technique (multiport network modelling coupled with cavity model), providing a detailed equivalent network representation of microstrip patches, mutual coupling among them, and the probe feed of an array has been used. It is a convenient framework for CAD of microstrip patch antennas composed of regular (rectangular, circular, elliptical, etc.) shape parts. The antenna operates at the two frequencies of the GPS signal with an axial ratio less than 3 dB over and angle 140 degrees and VSWR less than 1:1.5 over 20 MHz bandwidth centred on each band.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Results of an experiment to demonstrate the effectiveness of open-loop up-link power control for KU-band satellite links
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: With the open-loop control, a down-link signal from the satellite may be monitored at the transmitting earth station to obtain the fade level at that frequency, and this fade level is scaled to the up-link frequency. Provided the frequency difference between up- and down-links is not too large, frequency scaling of rain attenuation and other propagation effects can be accomplished with reasonable accuracy. An open-loop up-link power control system developed for Ku-band applications is described. The system was evaluated over a 12 month period on a transoceanic link between US and the Netherlands.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fade duration statistics: results from Olympus satellite
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors examine the characteristics of the duration statistics of rain fades at 12.5, 20 and 30 GHz as part of the Olympus satellite propagation experiment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The multipath channel transfer function dynamics: measurements and theoretical considerations
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Frequency selective fading due to multipath propagation is a major cause of impairment affecting line of sight digital radio relay links. In spite of the great interest devoted by many authors to the study of the static transfer function of the multipath channel, little material has been published on the dynamic of its characteristic parameters. Such information are needed for the improvement of existing performance prediction methods for digital radio relay links and for the equipment design such as equalizers and combiners. The basis of the article are the measurements performed on a digital radio link located in northern Italy. The transfer function is described in terms of the most relevant static and dynamic features and the parameters of the simplified three rays channel model are studied in connection to the experimental data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental and theoretical investigation of the effects of building scatter on site shielding
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors describe measurements of scattered microwave signals from a number of buildings made at 11.2 GHz. The scattering patterns observed at distances of a few hundred metres from the buildings were both dimension and distance dependent in nature. Conventional physical-optics considerations of far and near fields do not adequately account for these situations. The authors' computer analysis was based on Kirchoff method with a more precise physical-optics consideration. The analysis was extended to consider the effects of building surface conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design, manufacturing and testing of a Ku/Ka dichroic subreflector for space communications
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In the frame of an ESA-ESTEC Technological Development Program (ASTP-3), Alenia Spazio has designed, manufactured and qualified a 1 meter diameter dichroic subreflector for multifrequency antennas working at Ku and Ka frequency bands. A description of the configuration as well as design assumptions for electromagnetic and thermomechanical aspects are presented. The engineering efforts involved in materials selection and manufacturing processes are also presented. The most important results of the performed qualification campaign are presented for sinusoidal and random vibrations and thermal cycling tests. Furthermore a comparison between physical/ environmental requirements, predictions and achieved results is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An application of neural networks to the prediction of terrestrial wave propagation
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Field strength prediction is a central task for the planning of mobile communication systems. The decisive advantage in using neural networks for field strength predictions is given by the possibility of deriving training patterns directly from measurements. This allows the system to become very flexible and adapt to arbitrary environment. Owing to the highly parallel structure of the processing fast prediction systems seem to be possible in the future. First results of a training by measurement data show the feasibility of this approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resolution of multimoded HF transmissions using the DOSE superresolution direction finding algorithm
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Attempts to use the MUSIC algorithm to resolve multimoded ionospherically propagated signals failed due to the lack of robustness of MUSIC. A new algorithm DOSE (direction of arrival by signal elimination) is described, and its effectiveness evaluated from measurements made on a seven element array for a number of European broadcast transmissions in the range 9-10 MHz. This new superresolution method is very much better at resolving multimoded HF signals than interferometry and much more robust than MUSIC. In all cases, it was found that DOSE was able to resolve the received multi-component wave-field into separate modes which agreed well with those expected from a consideration of ionograms for the same period.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Millimeter wave antenna for limb sounding application
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The millimeter wave antenna study (MMWA) carried out under the ESTEC contract focused on antenna optimizations for a microwave limb sounding instrument for the middle atmosphere (10 to 100 km) which exploits four frequency bands, from 63 GHz for pressure retrieval up to 205 GHz for ozone. Six elliptical beams with +or-0.3 degrees scanning capability within the elevation plane were shown to be compliant with a tight beam efficiency specification of 96% inside the efficiency cone, defined by its apex angle to be 2.5 times the half-power beamwidth. Constant half-power beamwidths are needed within the frequency range with a 0.1 degrees value within the elevation plane and the highest value possible within the azimuth plane. The feasibility study showed that a 2.5 axial ratio was acceptable from the antenna design point of view, leading to a dual reflector antenna.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gain reduction of a shaped Cassegrain antenna due to lateral displacements
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The response of a 32-m radio telescope to tilts and lateral displacements of its components was analysed in the design phase, and the results of the analysis have now been confirmed by measurements with the completed antenna. The same analysis yielded a simple procedure to minimise the resultant reduction in gain by making compensating adjustments to the position and tilt of the subreflector. For antennas whose reflectors are conic sections, only the lateral displacement of the subreflector will normally require adjustment. For shaped antennas, however, it may be important to adjust the tilt also. This procedure has been successfully implemented to correct for the effects of gravitational distortion of the 32-m telescope as it is driven in elevation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prediction of water vapour attenuation on a slant path
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A new step-by-step procedure is presented for the estimation of satellite link water vapour attenuation on a slant path using temperature and humidity values at ground level as input parameters. An estimate for the standard deviation of the method is also given. Statistical maps for the water vapour scale height have been produced using numerical analysis of the ECMWF data. The water vapour scale height is needed in the method for correction of geographical variations of water vapour vertical profiles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design features of the ORION satellite antenna subsystem
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The ORION satellites (first launch 1994) will provide flexible, high capacity Ku-band communications between and within North America and Europe. Four-fold frequency re-use allows the provision of thirty-four transponders per spacecraft, with two-way networking traffic to 1.2 metre rooftop VSAT terminals. The author provides an overview of the communications antenna subsystem and highlights some of the novel and sophisticated design features. These include the following: numerically shaped, gridded reflectors, computer optimised multihorn feed geometry, feed coefficients optimised under mutual coupling, reconfigurable beams via on-board switching, very low thermal-distortion reflectors, novel sunshield design, and two-axis boresight trimming. Selected analyses and measurement results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prediction of rain attenuation at low-availabilities using models and data of widespread and convective rains
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The design of low-availability satellite communication systems operating at the frequencies above 10 GHz requires precise prediction of rain attenuation for annual outage time percentages greater than about 0.1%. The Leitao-Watson models (see IEE Proc. F, Commun. Radar Signal Process., vol.133, no.4, p.429-40, 1986) for widespread rain and convective rain are used for the calculation of mean cumulative distributions of rain attenuation. The effect of the melting layer, which exists above the widespread rain, is included in the calculations by using the model proposed by W. Zhang et al. (see Proceedings 20th European Microwave Conference, Stuttgart, Germany, p.1235-40, 1991). The mean distributions of 20 and 30 GHz rain attenuation are predicted for Jokioinen, Finland, in three cases: (1) rainfall consists of two rain types, and the melting layer exists above the widespread rain; (2) rain is merely of the widespread type having the melting layer above it; and (3) rain is only of the convective type without the melting layer. For Graz, Austria, the cumulative distributions of cases 2 and 3 are given. The results of each case are compared mutually and with atmospheric attenuation measured by radiometers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reduction of grating lobes in sequentially rotated microstrip patch arrays
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Sequentially rotated microstrip patch arrays are known to have severe grating lobe problems that limit the array bandwidth and the usefulness of linearly polarised elements. It is shown that grating lobe reduction can be achieved by applying rotation across larger than conventional, arrays. Examples are given that give up to 10 dB lobe reduction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Active microstrip antenna design with the simplified real frequency technique
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Presents a new approach for the design of amplifier-type active microstrip antennas by employing the concept of combining passive radiating patches and active devices for microwave signal transmission or reception. The simplified real frequency technique (SRFT) is introduced to design the lossless matching networks of active antennas. With this technique, there is no need to determine any form of equivalent circuit or analytical impedance function for the antennas and generators; the calculated or experimental data of the antennas and generators are processed directly. Furthermore, the need for choosing an algebraic transfer function as a measure of performance and the assumption of a topology for the matching networks in advance, which are common in most matching techniques, is avoided. The final results are optimised, physically realizable, normalized reflection coefficients that describe the matching networks. The matching networks are generally simpler and give superior gain properties compared to structures obtained by the analytic procedures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of mutual coupling and feed network on directivity and gain (array patch antennas)
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A detailed analysis of the influence of mutual coupling (MC) on the directivity and gain in array patch antennas is carried out. MC changes the active input impedances depending on the actual excitation currents of the array elements. In combination with the feed network this causes an increase of loss and a change of excitation currents. This is calculated by the multiport theory, where the antenna elements are represented by the mutual impedance matrix and the feed network is described by the transmission line theory. By changing the input impedances the input power is altered too. A formula is derived to determine the directivity enhancement of an nxn-array compared to a single element, if the MC is known. The theory is applied to 2*2- and 4*4-array patch antennas at 24.125 GHz+or-10% under consideration of dispersion effects of the microstrip feed network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error probability as a function of baudrate, time and operating frequency for HF radio links
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A computer algorithm was developed to calculate the error probability as a function of data rate (bps). time and frequency for a given HF-radio path. for a standard FSK signal. Also the Doppler-shift and the channel occupation was estimated for the radio link. In order to determine the error probability, the fading phenomenon was taken into account. A statistical approach was necessary-the 'random-walk method'-in which each mode was represented as a phasor with a constant magnitude, but random phase. The channel occupancy was determined via a mathematical model proposed by Laycock et. al. (1988). in which the spectral density between 2 and 30 MHz, obtained through measurements with a measuring receiver. was processed on a statistical basis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spacecraft antenna design and applications
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The evolution of satellite antennas in Europe and elsewhere has been impressive over the last decade. Whilst the authors treat this development with regard to the European scene, the advances and trends are globally common. The European Space Agency is actively engaged in the development of satellites and spacecraft for scientific, earth observation and communications missions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Melting layer studies at S band and comparisons with a physical model
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The transition from ice to water in precipitation systems, termed the melting layer, has an important impact on communications systems, through propagation effects, on meteorological radars, through enhanced scattering (the Bright Band), and on proposed space radars. Several melting layer models have been developed, often with different aims, but comparisons with measurements have been somewhat limited. The aim of the work presented in the paper is to begin to examine the currently available models, and where possible to compare their predictions with radar data. The much more difficult task of evaluating the ability of models to estimate path integrated quantities such as attenuation and Cross-polar Discrimination (XPD) is not attempted here, although this is a key application area for any model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Off-axis radiation-pattern calculation of a Cassegrain antenna system with an application to site shielding
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors have calculated the off-axis receiving pattern of a Cassegrain reflector antenna with a prescribed geometry as function of antenna azimuth in the absence as well as in the presence of a half-plane obstacle. The model used is based on GO and UTD and includes 21 wave contributions to calculate the total field at the feed. These contributions are individually traced through the antenna system and are spatially weighted by the feed pattern assumed. The ray analysis indicates that some of the individual contributions can be neglected to simplify the model. The model proposed analyses the combined problem of obstacle and antenna diffraction since in many cases the obstacle is in the near field of the earth-station antenna. Results of the additional attenuation caused by the presence of the obstacle on the propagation path of an interference source are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some problems associated with CCIB interference predictions: Indian experiences
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors deal with the problems in the prediction of interference levels over the Indian subcontinent using CCIR recommendations relating to tropospheric radiowave propagation. These have surfaced in the light of their experience in analysing some cases of interfering signals. They advocate a new integrated prediction procedure-as suggested by M.T. Hewitt for the UK-for tropical countries. (See Proceedings International Microwave Conference, Brazil, p.246-51, 1991). They present some experimental evidence from the Indian subcontinent for the support of the model proposed by Hewitt.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An active array for UHF compact range illumination
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The use of the reflector fed compact range for generating an approximation to a plane electromagnetic wave is well established for radiative EMC testing and for antenna measurements at frequencies in the GHz region. Extension of this technique into the VHF-UHF frequency range poses problems. In this frequency range control of the aperture illumination is better achieved by using an array antenna. Antenna arrays have the advantage that their dimensions may be smaller than those of a paraboloidal reflector over the frequency range of interest, since they are not limited by geometrical optics. A further advantage is that, by means of an active feed network, the size and quality of the quiet zone may be optimised to suit the geometry of the device under test. Such an active array has been developed at the University of Bradford and is described in the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Observations of HF signals propagated over high latitude paths
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A frequency agile transmitter has been installed within the polar cap at Clyde River, NWT, Canada (70 degrees N, 69 degrees W). Five receiving and data logging systems have been deployed to provide four transauroral paths and one path contained entirely within the polar cap region. Results from two receiving sites at Leicester, UK, and Boston, USA, during a one-month experimental campaign undertaken from 16 January to 10 February 1989, are used to illustrate some of the influences of the auroral oval and mid-latitude trough on HF propagation. The trough controls the time at which signals with frequencies between 18 and 23 MHz are lost in the evening. The auroral oval can give rise to night-time propagation of signals on frequencies much higher than the usual night-time MUF.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Propagation considerations on L-band handheld communication service offerings via satellite
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors discuss a series of experiments attempting to more clearly define the propagation characteristics of L-band signals in various kinds of environments under way at COMSAT Laboratories in Clarksburg, Maryland, USA. The experiments involve taking signal strength measurements of a 1.5 GHz pilot tone aboard an INMARSAT II satellite at 40 degrees elevation relative to Clarksburg. It has been found that wooded areas can produce from 5 to as much as 20 dB of signal attenuation. The human body can also produce up to 10 dB attenuation when blocking the signal path in close proximity to the receive antenna. Studies were also made from inside a building. The average received signal level for a clear direct path through an office window was found to be up to 6 dB less than the equivalent measurement in an outside open area. The window glass seemed to be the main attenuator, with probable interference from scatterers within the office.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Visibility estimation for urban radio-link design
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Point-to-multipoint networks acquire a great importance in modern communications due to their high data transmission capacity and installation flexibility. The planning of point-to-multipoint networks is strictly connected to the urban environment characteristics such as building heights and spatial distribution. Therefore, it is necessary to develop procedures which are able to provide the most important design factors. One of these is line-of-sight propagation path visibility. The paper describes a model based on the building density distribution for the urban area under study which provides the probability of visibility of a nodal station for a given urban area where the potential subscribers are located. If the method is applied to the radio coverage region, defined by the characteristics of the radio base station, then the efficiency of the system, in terms of visibility, can be evaluated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of a crank-line antenna
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors focus on a crank-line antenna located in free space, avoiding the use of a dielectric substrate. The antenna is backed by a perfectly conducting plane, (ground plane). The current distribution on the crank-line antenna is obtained using the method of moments, and the radiation characteristics are investigated. The effect of the antenna height above the ground plane on the radiation characteristics is also investigated. It is found that gain enhancement is realised by gradually increasing the antenna height above the ground plane. The comparison of the gain between two cases, with and without a gradual increase in the antenna height, is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Shape control experiment of on-board large mesh antenna reflector
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Describes an on-board shape control method and control results for a mesh antenna reflector of 4 m phi that is formed on a folding truss structure. Antenna patterns calculated using experimental data are also shown and the effectiveness of the proposed method is confirmed from the restoration of antenna gain and pointing direction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of the impact of cloud induced scintillations on satellite links
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Cloud induced scintillations affect Earth-space paths above about 10 GHz. These scintillation effects would create very serious problems on future satellite communication systems at millimeter waves, especially with small receiving antennas and on low elevation links. Based on a few years measurements, a model for cloud produced scintillations has been developed and validated. It predicts the influence of various link parameters both on the scintillation time-series and on the channel transfer functions during realistic turbulent events.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Superquadric loop antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A unified formulation is presented which allows modeling of a continuum of different loop geometries, including circular, square, and folded dipole configurations, through use of the superquadric curve. The analysis includes the case of two superquadric loops with arbitrary geometries, excitation, and relative orientation to allow determination of the effects of mutual coupling on the antenna characteristics. A Galerkin type moment method using piecewise sinusoidal basis and weighting functions is used to solve an electric field integral equation (EFIE) for thin wires. A novel parametrization for the superquadric curve is given which allows the use of curved wire segments, rather than the commonly employed linear segments, to construct the antenna geometry. The concept of antenna diversity is discussed and the diversity performance of coupled superquadric loop antennas is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effectiveness of tape treatment in improving the performance of a panelled CATR at millimetre waves
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The panelled approach is the technique usually adopted for the construction of the reflector(s) of a compact antenna test range (CATR) in order to fulfil the requirements of high surface accuracy needed for millimetre wave operation. However diffraction due to the edges of the interpanel gaps can affect the radiation pattern measurement accuracy by the formation of spurious lobes. In an attempt to rectify the situation a thin metallic tape can be used in order to cover the gap. This approach has been studied experimentally. The potential of improvement has been demonstrated, but this approach does not lead automatically to the complete elimination of the problems caused due to the discontinuity of the reflector surface at the interpanel junctions. Some results of a theoretical study concerning the tape induced scattering are presented in order to provide a realistic view about the effectiveness of tape treatment mainly at the 180 GHz bands.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Focal plane dielectric rod arrays with printed launchers
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A novel antenna structure is proposed which combines features of both dielectric rod and vivaldi antennas and has some attractions for use in focal plane arrays. Its sampling performance is better than for the known fully printed types, though not as good as can be achieved by rod arrays with waveguide launchers. The structure combines good features of the two fully printed types. It has considerably lower cross polarisation than continuous width slot antennas arrays, but a bandwidth as least as good. Although the new antenna is not a fully printed one, it does remove most of the disadvantages of waveguide launchers. It can be relatively easily mass replicated and integrated with MIC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nearfield structure of impulse driven, tubular, thick dipoles
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The impedance behaviour of electrical dipoles can be well described by the model of R. Sato and M. Sato (1984). It uses a transmission line section with load sections located at either termination. Each load contains lumped elements. i.e. inductance and resistors, thus describing the effects of the feeding region and the dipole tip on the current. The time dependant nearfields of thick tubular dipoles, given for the cases of a voltage impressed impulse generator and of a high impedance generator, are compared with these of more idealized (thinner) dipoles. From a two wire model the effects of thickness are explained and partly related to an equivalent circuit. It is shown, that the assumption, that radiation is provoked only by the feeding point and the dipole tips is not valid for thick dipoles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compact active patch antenna
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors describe an original active patch antenna in which the whole bias circuit, transistor, decoupling circuit and the patch element form a structure which is not bigger than a passive antenna. A compact amplifier circuit composed of a transistor placed on the same face as the radiating patch and a bias circuit etched in the ground plane ensures a high gain and a low loss for the realized antenna. Some precautions have been taken so that the radiation pattern is not affected and the cross polarization level doesn't have to be raised. This element can be used in active array antennas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental results for metal-strip-loaded image-guide antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Theoretical and experimental results are presented for a planar leaky-wave antenna that consists of an image-guide periodically loaded with metal strips on its top surface. This kind of antennas are very attractive for millimeter wave applications, because their low cost, small size and ease of manufacture, using integrated circuit technology. The mode-matching technique together with the effective dielectric constant (EDC) method have been used to analyze the antenna and to design the prototypes. Mode-matching, based on a space harmonic expansion of the fields in each region, is used to analyze accurately the structure with infinite lateral extent, taking into account the thickness of the metal strips. This method is extended by using the EDC approach to analyze the finite width antenna. The method one allows to obtain the fields inside and outside the antenna, the phase and leaky constants, beta and alpha , and the radiation patterns. The authors present careful measured data for several prototypes, and show that the theory developed previously is accurate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modal approach for the analysis of the aperture-coupled multi-layer microstrip array
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Microstrip array antennas consisting of printed elements integrated with feed network and active circuits in multiple dielectric layers are assuming an important role for telecommunication applications. The main consideration which supports the multi-layer architecture for microstrip antennas is to separate the radiator and the feed sections by means of a ground plane with coupling apertures, in order to avoid the interference of the feed network on the radiation of the patches. The complexity of the microstrip array configuration, in terms of involved geometries and design parameters, requires a versatile and powerful electromagnetic approach for a both accurate and time limited analysis of the structure. The theoretical model description and the validation measurements are the subject of the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of cross polar discrimination in circularly and linearly polarized reflector antennas with surface imperfections
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Apart from loss in gain, one other outcome of surface errors on the performance of reflector antennas is to introduce cross-polarization along the boresight. It is the objective of the author investigates the effect of surface aberrations on the performance of axisymmetric reflector antennas employing circular and linear polarizations. Furthermore, the effect of regional variations in the surface tolerance on the cross polarization characteristics are also studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel circularly polarised printed antenna
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Proposes a novel printed antenna that is capable of yielding circular polarisation. The antenna consists of a planar slow-wave structure, which has waveguiding properties similar to those of a circular helix. The slow-wave structure can be fabricated using printed circuit techniques. For a suitable mode and optimum dimensions, analysis indicates two symmetric circularly polarised beams at 32 degrees with respect to the endfire direction. The analytical results are presented together with preliminary experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Antenna pattern interpolation by generalized Whittaker reconstruction
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Whittaker reconstruction is an effective tool for interpolation of band limited data. Whittaker (1915) originally introduced the interpolation formula termed the cardinal functions as the function that represents a set of equispaced samples but has no periodic components of period less than twice the sample spacing. The method is a useful tool in the analysis and design of multiple beam reflector antenna systems. A good description of the method has been given by Bucci et al. (1980). The authors discuss some problems encountered with the method and their solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diagnostics of an SSR array antenna from the measured near-field intensity using phase retrieval
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A new possibility for array diagnostics is to apply the phase retrieval approach. It is now established that the aperture phase of a reflector antenna and its complex aperture field can be determined from scans of the radiated or received intensity patterns. It is envisaged that such a measurement procedure, which dispenses with the reference channel therefore removing the requirement for access to the antenna system under test, might be applied to operational antennas, for example, to diagnose the condition of a radar array in service. A phase retrieval algorithm to recover the discrete source distribution of array antennas has been formulated and applied to the diagnosis of a waveguide array by Lord et al. (see IEE Proc. H, vol.139, no.4, p.392, 1992). In the paper the algorithm is applied to scan cylindrical near-field data of a Marconi secondary surveillance radar (SSR) antenna.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VHF horizontally-polarized antennas for aircraft
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Apart from a few military applications, the only VHF horizontally-polarized systems in general use on aircraft are those for the navigation aids ILS (instrument landing system) and VOR (VHF omni-range). As these are used on all but the smallest civil aircraft and on many military ones, antenna solutions have been produced for a wide range of aircraft size and shapes. Two classes of antennas are discussed, giving omniazimuth and directional coverage respectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: General model of a planar antenna
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Presents a general modelling method of a planar antenna element for determining the directivity and the impedance properties of the single antenna element and the antenna array. The radiation effect of a planar antenna is dependent on the fringing field between microstrip patch edge and the ground plane. The fringing field distribution around the planar patch edge is determined by the linear form of the wave equation in which the Green's function approach was applied. The multiport model of dependence between the current excitation of the planar antenna and the voltage distribution surrounding the planar element is described in a matrix form which consists of column matrices of the edge voltage distribution and current excitation, and a square impedance matrix of the mutual impedance between ports of the model. The computational procedure of the general model is outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Slow-wave analysis on double layered substrates (microstrip lines)
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Full wave analysis of a slow-wave microstrip transmission line on a ferromagnetic semiconductor with an insulator is presented. A spectral domain method with sampling theorem is used. A new current distribution is applied. The obtained slow-wave factor is higher than that when only lossless ferromagnetic material is used. Phase shifting is also achieved by the structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prediction of the radiation pattern of phased array antennas using modified S-parameter measurements
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors show that the conventional S-parameter radiation pattern prediction technique produces significant pattern errors which can be accounted for by re-radiation terms. These terms are easily determined through a series of S-parameter measurements. The technique is demonstrated on a three element array, but will also be applicable to larger arrays.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model for trans-horizon propagation in the low-VHF band
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors identify the dominant mode of propagation on BLOS (beyond line of sight) paths up to 400 km in range at frequencies in the low-VHF band as tropospheric reflection. The CCIR model which is the most widely used troposcatter loss prediction model consistently gave optimistic values for the long term transmission loss compared with the measured loss at 47 MHz over channels between 100 km and 400 km in length. The main reason for this was because although the measured instantaneous signal levels were in rough agreement with predicted values, the time that the signal was present was not i.e., it was present for less than 50% of the time. This was especially true when the system was operating on the upper range limit of the propagation mechanism. The major limitation of the current theoretical tropospheric reflection models is that because they assume static atmospheric conditions, the short term fading, which is caused by the movement between reflecting layers is not taken into account.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sensitivity of tri-linear refractivity models to perturbations in refractivity
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Previous work has shown that when a well defined stratified layer exists over several tens of kilometres, so that the troposphere possesses a high degree of horizontal homogeneity, the refractivity is well approximated by a tri-linear profile and that using this approximation leads to good agreement between measured attenuations and those obtained by solution of the parabolic wave equation. The most common method of obtaining refractivity data is through the measurement of the meteorological parameters, pressure. temperature and humidity. However, the turbulent nature of the troposphere, combined with the resolution of the measurement sensors, places an upper limit on the accuracy to which the refractivity profile can be determined. Therefore it is important to quantify the effect of these inaccuracies on the solutions of the parabolic wave equation. and hence, the work presented in the paper, investigates the sensitivity of the predicted signal level to small perturbations in the refractivity profile.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple model applied to the analysis of E-plane and H-plane mutual coupling between microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The study of mutual coupling between microstrip patches is useful to design arrays of this kind of antennas, where the spacing between elements are less than a wavelength. Coupling between a patch and its neighbours must be computed to find the impedance matrix relating currents and voltages in the array. Microstrip patches are represented by magnetic current lines using the cavity model (CM). The theoretical model presented is useful to predict the coupling levels between microstrip antennas, and it has been developed for two basic configurations (E-plane and H-plane). The method shows enough accuracy when the substrate height is small in terms of wavelengths, as required by CM. The required computing time is very little in comparison with other methods (full-wave models, extended CM, reaction principle with exact Green's functions), methods that don't ensure total accuracy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of adaptive arrays based on element position perturbations
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Null steering in adaptive arrays by element position perturbations has been investigated. The results showed that it is possible to steer array nulls in the directions of interfering signals by perturbing the element positions of linear arrays, provided that the number of interfering signals is less than half the number of array elements. Arrays with different number of elements and various illumination functions were investigated. The main advantage of using this technique over the other commonly used methods is that the amplitudes and phases of the array elements can be used mainly to steer the main beam towards the desired signal. The authors report on the design of a digital feedback control system to provide null steering by controlling the array element positions automatically. The array comprises a signal processor, digital control algorithm (PID), stepper motors, shaft encoders, actuators and multiplexers. The proposed adaptive system is used to form automatically the required nulls in the direction of arrival of the interference. The design has been tested on arrays of three, five and eight elements. The simulation results show the effectiveness of this technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Array fed dual reflector synthesis for multiple beams
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Requirements for antennas to provide multiple or scanned beams over a limited angular sector, are encountered in both satellite and radar applications. In such cases the hybrid antenna, consisting of one or two reflectors illuminated by a small phased array, can provide a cost effective and flexible solution. The authors describe a new synthesis method for such configurations, which allows all of the design requirements to be addressed. The technique is quite general, but has initially been implemented in two dimensions, where scanning is considered only in the offset plane of the reflectors. The synthesis of a single beam antenna is described. This forms the basis of an iterative procedure for the synthesis of the multiple beam systems. Four design examples are considered, covering cases where the power distribution over the main reflector aperture may be equal to, or different to that over the feed array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Underlying surface remote sensing optimal algorithms and accuracy by proper radiation
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: For dissipated surfaces investigated by means of remote sensing (RS) with the help of active and passive radar systems the determination of the experimental conditions providing the best qualitative measurement results becomes necessary. A solution is given for a number of surface conditions and electrodynamic parameters estimation identity problems where the latter ones are functionally connected with signal models received in the given polarization basis by the solution of electrodynamic direct problems. The algorithms and accuracy of the optimal parameters estimation of the proper radiation surface electrodynamic models were found by maximum likelihood function. Here the mathematic thermodynamic temperature dependencies on the desired parameters for the flat small-scale, large-scale and two-scale surface approaching small perturbation and Kirhof approximations are used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Phasing effects of cascaded and spatially varying planar arrays
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The paper deals with some procedures for attaining controlled modifications of the incident field that result in beam direction, filtered and focused radiation patterns. Planar single and multilayer spatially varying array designs have been incited to produce the required combination of amplitude and phase changes. A number of prototypes (of up to four layers) have been manufactured and experimentally assessed in the 26-40 GHz frequency region. The bandwidth and polarisation performance are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The accuracy of VHF/UHF field strength prediction
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author discusses field-strength prediction methods for VHF/UHF. Topics discussed include the development of field strength prediction; the need for definitions for prediction accuracy; analysis of prediction accuracy; and prospects for the improvement of empirical methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New concept of virtual polarisation adaptation
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Presents the possibility of an alternative approach to the problem of clutter cancellation by applying a real receiving vector which could not be radiated by physically realizable antenna, or would not be obtained as vectorial equivalent of a positively semifinite hermitian coherency matrix of a target, but could be strictly perpendicular to the vector of incident disturbance causing its complete cancellation. The limitations of hitherto known methods are discussed for the case of polarimetric on receive radar and then the idea of a new optimum receiver using the new concept of virtual polarisation adaptation is demonstrated. The reception of partially polarized disturbances and signals can best explained by the Stokes four-sphere in four-dimensional real space of the Stokes parameters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Correlation of transhorizon signal level strength with localised surface meteorological parameters
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The paper examines the dependence of path loss on different meteorological parameters. These parameters are the localised surface temperature, pressure, and humidity measured at the receiver sites. The seasonal and diurnal variations of path loss are also presented to illustrate its changes throughout the day and seasons. This information is important in designing and planning radio links and numerical values of the cumulative distribution are presented. It shows that the maximum daily temperature averaged over a period of 1 to 2 weeks, is the most reliable meteorological parameter for path loss prediction. The conditional probability between path loss level and maximum daily temperature P(L mod T) is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of an adaptive array for interference cancelling based on KLT and singular value decomposition
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors study the performance of an LMS based adaptive array. First they consider the performance of this array for a sudden interference encountered during adaptation and demonstrate that the speed of the convergence of this adaptive system is dependent on the eigenvalue spread of the autocorrelation matrix of the input data to the array elements. The transform domain LMS algorithm was developed by S.S. Narayan et al. (1983). The speed of the convergence of the LMS algorithm can be significantly improved by choosing appropriate transform.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast convergent method for the evaluation of scattered near-field from underground cylindrical scatterers
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Certain methods of identification of underground targets are based on the knowledge of scattered near field. The evaluation of the near field is always numerically cumbersome, but near field carries more information about a scatterer. A method is proposed to overcome the significant difficulties arising from the numerical evaluation of Fourier type integrals. For simplicity of analysis the authors consider cylindrical scatterers of infinite length. The simplest physical model for the description of the environment (soil and air) is the one layer model for the structure of the ground. Numerical results are obtained and presented for the VHF band.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Arrays of stub loaded inductive strips
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The transmission properties of multilayer arrays of resonant elements have been discussed in the open literature from time to time, often emphasising the improved passband edge ratios that can be obtained relative to those available from single layers. Passbands extending below 10 GHz often require conductor widths less than 0.2 mm. Still finer lines have increased mechanical stability problems. Munk et al. (1971) used inductive stubs to load the dipole elements. The paper summarises results from a study of strip arrays loaded periodically with stubs to further increase the equivalent inductance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance and design of steerable antenna feed assembly for X-band payloads
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An X-band steerable antenna assembly was required as part of the antenna farm subsystem for the X-band payload equipment used on satellites like HISPASAT. The design chosen for this antenna assembly uses a single feed horn to illuminate a steerable offset parabolic reflector. This system produces a moveable spot beam which may be aimed towards any point on the Earth's surface visible to the spacecraft. The steerable antenna feed assembly (SAFA) has to withstand the increased vibration requirements resulting from its position on top of the mast. The SAFA consists of a profiled corrugated horn, a polariser, an ortho-mode transducer, two waveguide runs, mechanical and electrical interfaces, thermal control hardware and an alignment cube. The actual alignment adjustment system was mounted between the SAFA and the mast. The paper describes the performance requirements, design, manufacture and test of this feed assembly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent advances in the measurement of precipitation by radar
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The phase is important for predicting attenuation on communication links. For meteorological and hydrological application, the rainfall rate at the ground (R in mm/hr) is estimated using an empirical relationship of the form: Z=200 R/sup 1.6/ An ice sphere has a value of Z which is 7 dB less than the same size liquid water sphere; when a low density ice particle starts to melt it reflects microwaves like a giant raindrop and Z may 10 dB higher than for the equivalent raindrop. Values of R from equation 1 are prone to error, due to, for example: variation in the raindrop size distribution, the enhanced return from melting snowflakes ('the bright band'), overshooting of the low level precipitation at large ranges, the presence of large hailstones and ground clutter, and the spurious returns due to anomalous propagation. The author considers how polarisation parameters can be used to provide additional information on the types of precipitation present. The survey concentrates on the parameters derived from radiation linearly polarised in the horizontal and vertical directions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer simulation of tomographic problems
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The computer modelling program package developed can be applied in all fields of tomography. Using this program package for computer simulation, it is possible to choose the registration scheme, to estimate the effects of distortions and noise, to find a suitable method of preliminary data processing, to find the optimal reconstruction system configuration using different criteria, and to evaluate the quality of the reconstruction of the internal structure of an object. Evidently all these possibilities are of great scientific value, however the package is above all intended for academic applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of obstacles on interference between slant paths and terrestrial links, as a function of frequency
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Questions related to interference between radio communication systems are becoming more and more crucial as both terrestrial and satellite radio services are rapidly expanding. This interference can be reduced by several techniques, in particular site shielding (COST Project 210). In this method, an obstacle is used in the vicinity of an earth station to be protected against unwanted signals produced by terrestrial links.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of microstrip loop antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A number of mobile satellite systems are proposed for service in the late 1990s. A study of concentric annular ring arrays is reported in which the rings are excited in various modes, resulting in toroidal beams pointing at different elevation angles. Switching between modes can provide a degree of beam steering. The gain of a single patch was 5-7 dB typically. However, this was found to be sensitive to the size of the ground plane on which it was mounted and this variation in gain has been investigated. A theoretical study is presented of a 4 element stacked array of concentric ring elements in which a degree of beam steering is attained by switching modes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A coaxial feed system integrated within a Cassegrain subreflector
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Describes a low-frequency feed fitted inside the subreflector of a Cassegrain antenna. One such facility has been added to a 13-metre Cassegrain (GB13C) to enable it to work simultaneously in L-band (1.525-1.6605 GHz) and C-band (3.60-4.20/5.85-6.454 GHz). The radiating element is an annular slot inset into the subreflector surface and fed by a coaxial matching network carrying the TE/sub 11/ mode. The design of the TE/sub 11/ mode coaxial matching network was carried out using mode-matching software written for the purpose and including an accurate model for the self-admittance of the coaxial aperture. Dielectric loading was used at the aperture and at one other point in the network for mechanical reasons. A coaxial low pass filter is placed within the network. This was also designed using the mode matching software and is necessary to ensure high rejection of the C-band transmit band power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The new L/K-band polarimeter system for the 32 m radiotelescope at Cambridge
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A new 32 m Cassegrain radio telescope has been added to Jodrell Bank's MERLIN network. For wavelengths of 6 cm and less, conical corrugated feed horns have been employed with excellent results, both in terms of aperture efficiency and system noise temperature. Furthermore such feeds perform well in the reception of circularly polarized waves, an essential requirement for MERLIN. A low-cost alternative to the conical corrugated horn has been sought. The 'diagonal horn' was identified as a possible candidate and investigations have been carried out into its suitability as a low-cost 20 cm horn, using scale models at 6 cm and 1.3 cm wavelengths. The authors describe the diagonal horn design and polarization characteristics and compare the radiotelescope performance at 6 cm with diagonal and corrugated horns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of the number of noise eigenvectors used and quantisation errors on the performance of the MUSIC algorithm
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors show that quantisation errors reduce the resolution of the MUSIC algorithm, and that the loss in performance is significant if less than 14 bit digitization is used. However, in practice other system errors will make the ADC requirements less stringent and 12 bit ADCs (which will provide 10 to 11 bit quantization in a practical system) should give adequate performance, since quantization errors will still not be the main cause of loss of performance. It is also shown that not all the noise subspace eigenvectors need be used to produce the MUSIC spectrum, and that using less than all the noise subspace eigenvectors will improve performance and robustness, while also reducing computation. Use of just one noise subspace eigenvector is not recommended in practice, since no averaging down of spurious cusps in the spectrum occurs, leading to false results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Square waveguide loaded with lossy magnetic material in the B-plane walls
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The geometry of the loaded rectangular waveguide lends itself for a rigorous hybrid mode analysis. However, in the literature there are no published numerical results of the application of such analysis on the rectangular waveguide with lossy magnetic coating in the E-plane walls. The propagation and radiation characteristics of a square waveguide with a lossy magnetic coating in the E-plane walls (perpendicular to the E field of the TE/sub 10/ mode) are evaluated numerically extending a rigorous hybrid-mode approach previously used for the rectangular waveguide loaded with dielectric slabs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: COST Project 235 activities on radiowave propagation effects on next-generation fixed-service terrestrial telecommunication systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Three COST projects on tropospheric radiowave propagation topics have been conducted during the 20 years existence of COST and a fourth is now in operation. This fourth project is mainly concerned with wideband paths and millimetre wavelengths, and an interim report has been produced. The paper outlines the objectives and progress to date; it also outlines the successes of earlier projects in the series.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mobile systems; from chaos to convergence (radio communication)
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author discusses the benefits of the development of international standards for mobile radio systems to replace national standards. Progress made towards this in Europe is discussed. Topics covered include GSM; DECT; the RACE initiative; and issues for antennas and propagation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coupling of antenna fields to planar microstrip transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors present a computer model to study the response of a lossy coupled microstrip interconnect illuminated by an electromagnetic field generated by an in the farfield zone. The model allows the computation of currents and voltages induced by the antenna fields of arbitrary angle of incidence and polarization at any point along the coupled microstrip line, which is terminated in passive loads at both ends. The effects of high substrate permittivity and loss tangent on the coupling of the antenna fields into the microstrip is investigated in detail. The author also presents a model for the coupling of the antenna fields to the microstrip when the line is placed in the near field zone of the antenna and the fields are highly nonuniform. The exact formulas for the wave coupling in this specific case contain complicated integrals which can not be evaluated analytically and numerical procedures are used to obtain the final results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Impact of mutual coupling in arrays of non-contacting circular horns
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Describes a mode matching approach of analysing array mutual coupling where the fields in both the circular waveguide apertures and the fields in the interstice of the non-contacting horns are represented as a sum of modes. The approach is due to Bird (see IEE Conf. Antennas Propag. ICAP, p.849, 1991 and IEE J. Microwaves Opt. Acoust., p.172, 1979) with an extension to include the modes of the multiconductor transmission line formed by the exterior surfaces of the horns. It is outlined, and some illustrative results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of offset double torus dual-beam antenna by minimizing aperture mapping distortion
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Dual-beam earth station antennas which track two satellites simultaneously have been developed for the Japanese public telecommunication network systems. The dual-beam earth station antenna is an offset double torus antenna with two auxiliary-reflectors that can be used for the 30/20 GHz band and has a good commercial record of performance. The authors describe a reflector system design scheme that minimizes the aperture mapping distortion of an offset double torus antenna with two auxiliary-reflectors. In order to achieve higher aperture efficiency and higher XPD (cross polarization discrimination), the double torus configuration is optimized and the transformation of nondistorted mapping is applied to all reflectors including the two auxiliary-reflectors. The relation between the antenna geometrical parameters and the distortion of aperture mapping is studied. The validity of this design scheme is verified by the experimental results gained from a fabricated offset double torus dual-beam antenna operating in the 14/12 GHz band.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer modelling of superconducting helical antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Computer modelling of a parasitically-driven normal-mode helical antenna is reported. This structure is particularly suitable for realisation with superconductor, but attempts to model it using standard method-of-moments techniques are very prone to instability. A new moment-method program was written using polynomial basis functions and selective use of the exact thin-wire kernel. This gave stable results even in the region of very sharp resonance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast synthesis of shaped reflector antennas for contoured beams
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author describes and exemplifies a technique for aperture synthesis and shaped reflector design which has most of the accuracy and flexibility of the analysis-in-an-optimisation-loop design method, while being many times faster. The algorithm is a version of the Method of Successive Projections. The author emphasises practical applications for satellite antennas; discussion focusses on single offset reflectors and on the application of the algorithm to multiple simultaneous requirements, such as multiple beams or multiple frequencies. An example is shown of the synthesis of a C-band transmit/receive antenna exhibiting true dual-band performance with a coverage specification including isolation as well as in-coverage gain requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of GTD with compensation theorem for finite size knife edges
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The application of the geometrical theory of diffraction to radio wave scattering by edges which are infinitely long is well established. The technique has also been applied successfully to edges which are relatively short in terms of wavelengths, but no quantitative measure has previously been available to say how the error increases as the length of the edge decreases. In contrast, the compensation theorem is a perturbation technique which increases in accuracy as the size of the perturbing structure gets smaller. A comparison has therefore been carried out between the results of the two approaches, applied to radiowave propagation over a finite height and finite width rectangular conducting plate. In the associated experiments the heights of the transmitter and receiver were kept at ground level, to simplify both the analysis and the experimental operating procedure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of ground conductivity in Bahrain by the ground-wave attenuation method
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors discusses the measurement of equivalent ground conductivity, which plays an important role in ground-wave radio transmission. The author concludes that the humidity (moisture content) of soils is a major factor in determining the conductivity values. Measurements of conductivity as a function of moisture content show very low values for dried samples, compared with moistened ones. There is no significant diurnal or seasonal variation. The author believes this is due to the fact that Bahrain is a sand dominated country, and sand is moisture-regain sensitive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of interference suppression radome for microstrip arrays
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: New design concepts are described for improving the performance of a cheap, lightweight radome cover for facilitating interference suppression, in particular for microstrip antennas. The antenna structure presented consists of a microstrip planar array fitted with a lossy sheet and separated by a foam spacer. The spacer thickness is crucial to the design and must be chosen such that d+h is a multiple of lambda /2 to ensure that any loss in antenna gain is minimised at the antenna transmission frequency. The lossy sheet gives some useful isolation properties for out-of-band interference but gives no protection at the transmission band. Therefore it is important that this null is limited to a narrow bandwidth and that the antenna radiation pattern is largely unaffected by the radome presence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The ACTS propagation campaign
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The Advanced Communications Technology Satellite (ACTS) is the core of a NASA experiment to advance the state-of-the-art in satellite communications. The quality of data from the ACTS experiments will depend on how accurately rain-fade statistics and fade dynamics can be measured in order to derive an appropriate algorithm that will combat fading for links using small terminals. To address propagation concerns of ACTS and other Ka-band satellites of the future, NASA is sponsoring a propagation campaign which includes seven data collection sites at geographically diverse locations in North America. The author reviews the planning process, hardware development, and measurement program involved in the forthcoming ACTS propagation experiments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scanning properties of superdirective antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Investigates, the scanning properties of superdirective array functions, which is essential in applications where the main beam has to be steered. Many examples can be found in the applications related to phased and adaptive arrays. The study shows that the superdirective properties of the array are maintained over an extremely small scan angle range of the main beam, beyond which the array pattern collapses. These results apply when the main beam scanning is generated through the use of the progressive phase shift. It has also been found that the superdirective array properties can be maintained over an appreciable scan angle, if the array illumination function is readjusted with the scan angle. Examples of the steered superdirective pattern are given for an eleven-element two-wavelength array. The narrow main beam is maintained over a scan angle of +or-20/sup 0/, while the side lobe level is maintained at the prescribed level.
