The results confirm that efficient superdirective functions can be used in applications where the main beam is to be scanned around the boreside direction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-order modes of two-scale nonuniform waveguide
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: It is well known that the waves of the lowest orders in an nonuniform waveguide can be described by the parabolic equation if the following conditions are fulfilled: kappa =kB>>1, v=B/L>>1, kappa v= sigma =kB/sup 2//L approximately 1. Here k=2 pi / lambda is the wave number, B is the characteristic width of the longitudinal nonuniformity. Here, it is implied the range D to be of the order of L. The authors derive an approximate description of lower-order modes of a two-scale nonuniform waveguide. They are submitted to a parabolic equation containing an additional term that gives an integral correction to the wave phase of the order 1/v at great distances X approximately D. This correction determined by the condition of removing secular (growing in X) terms in the asymptotic expansion can be evaluated by two-scale perturbation theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent developments in propagation counter-measures for VSAT services
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The need to provide open VSAT networks mandates that links meet agreed international standards. These standards fall into two categories: performance and availability. Performance objectives define the requirements for a connection over the bulk of the period it is in use. For satellite systems, this equates to clear sky conditions. Availability objectives refer to signal thresholds below which an outage is declared. A 'degraded performance' region exists between these objectives where the link can still be maintained, but at less than the designed quality. The margin between clear sky and degraded performance is small for VSATs and it is often difficult to separate performance and availability issues as they relate to propagation impairments. These aspects are considered below and some new results supporting impairment counter-measure investigations are given. The possible direction for counter-measures in VSAT systems is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Amplitude statistics of HF signal and noise on a 2300 km path over Europe
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors describe results of the analysis of signal fading and noise from a campaign of measurements over a 2300 km path between the UK and Greece for a range of frequencies from 7 to 20 MHz. The campaign was part of an experiment undertaken by RAL to study all aspects of fading at HF which are relevant to service planning. Improvements in standards for reliability and compatibility determination require further knowledge of signal and noise amplitude variability. Results are presented on within-an-hour and day-to-day variations, after a comprehensive study of the amplitude probability distributions of both signal and noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precision antenna measurements employing an outdoor cylindrical near-field test facility
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A state-of-the-art cylindrical near-field antenna test facility has been described which exhibits the performance of an indoor facility but is located outdoors. This facility has been developed to fully characterise a wide variety of large, complex antennas both in the far-field and at the aperture. The acceptance test philosophy has also been discussed, and a brief summary of the current status given. The development of this facility is a significant step forward for near-field testing of antennas, and helps to demonstrate the potential of this technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimisation of wall tapers in airborne radomes
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Describes a design method in which an established radome analysis package is used in conjunction with a conjugant gradient optimisation method to choose the wall taper. Example results are given for a radome whose shape has been chosen by the author to be representative of airborne designs although it is not drawn from any particular aircraft.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Figure-of-merit of ionospheric maps for use in propagation assessments
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Despite the intuitive feelings by the originators of the URSI maps of their superiority, the CCIR community could not be convinced to adopt these as a replacement for the maps already in use. The position today remains unchanged. Although there are no international efforts under way to generate further global maps, some studies are known to be in train to produce improved regional maps, in particular geographical areas. So this points to the need to review critically the adopted map-testing procedure. The paper makes proposals through the use of appropriate weighting factors to allow comparisons involving a mix of different types of measurement data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reflection of microwave LOS signal from rough surface in presence of surface duct
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A theoretical analysis of multipath fading due to the presence of surface duct and reflection from a rough surface, using local mode theory and grating theory is given. The surface roughness is modelled by a periodic function in one dimension. Numerical results of space diversity are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterisation of radio transmissions into and within buildings
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Previously reported measurements of radio propagation into and within buildings at 900, 1800 and 2300 MHz, have established that the Rayleigh-plus-log-normal model can describe successfully the statistical distribution of the received signal within buildings. A multiple regression analysis method is used to predict the signal path loss encountered by radio transmissions into and within buildings at these frequencies. Statistical methods have also been used in order to determine the reliability of the prediction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency selective surfaces with very low loss and cross-polarisation levels
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces have been used to increase the capacity of multifrequency reflector antenna systems by means of dichroic subreflectors. In modem satellite communications, multifrequency antennas need a quite low cross-polarisation level to cope with frequency reuse requirements and dichroic surfaces with low-losses are necessary in a cascade configuration to separate several frequency bands. The authors describe the design of an inductive frequency selective surface with a separation between transmission and reflection frequency bands of 1:1.2 and with very low loss and cross-polarisation levels. The design criteria for the choice of the proper lattice, the number of grids, the spacing among them and the geometry of the selective element are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Worst month rain statistics for the south of Spain
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An extensive study of rainfall records from a large number of meteorological stations located in every region of Iberia is being carried out in order to elaborate a rain intensity map based on local data. A statistical analysis was performed on data from several sites in Andalusia which showed that rainfall rates behaviour is strongly related to orographic and climatological features. The authors discuss the application of the CCIR worst month model and of the exponential CCIR model for the monthly fraction of excess. The results achieved show a high correlation to climatological characteristics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive sidelobe nulling using limited phase control
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A technique for synthesizing the null in the sidelobe region of an arbitrarily-shaped antenna pattern has been developed, with the null formed by perturbing the phases of 2 or 3 elements or subarrays of an array or subzones of a continuous aperture. By combining the principle of this technique with a suitable numerical minimization algorithm, it has been shown that it is possible to adaptively form a null in the direction of an interfering source, with relatively rapid and robust convergence. This adaptive algorithm requires no a priori knowledge of either the location of the interfering source or the antenna beam shape, and should be applicable to a wide class of antennas including phased arrays and reconfigurable mesh reflector antennas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Software for analysing coupling between antennas on a satellite or other platforms
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The important characteristics of any multiinstrument satellite design in respect of electromagnetic compatibility are the relative size and proximity of antennas, their operating frequencies, the harmonic frequencies at which they may respond, and the type of antenna configuration. This is particularly important when a relatively large number of antennas are in close vicinity of each other. Earth observation satellites such as the European Space Agency's Earth Resources Satellite (ERS-1) and Polar Earth Observation Mission (POEM-1) are good examples. The frequency range of the antennas is large and can extend from 100 MHz to 200 GHz. ERA has developed computer software which enables consideration of electromagnetic coupling between various antennas mounted on a complex platform. The authors describe the scope and capabilities of the software and give some comparison with measured results which have been carried out on mock-up of a satellite representing ERS-1. Some results of computation performed recently for POEM 1 are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tomographic imaging of electron density in the auroral ionosphere
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Computerised tomography involves the measurement of the line integral of a parameter along many intersecting ray paths with inversion of the resultant data to give a two-dimensional image of the parameter. In ionospheric tomography, the total electron content is measured with the reconstruction yielding electron density in a cross-section through the ionosphere. The paper reports results from a campaign of experimental observations made in Scandinavia in which the tomographic images of electron density have been compared with measurements obtained from a specially designed scan of the EISCAT radar. The 'ground truth' observations by the radar provide verification of the tomographic technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fading patterns and physical mechanisms associated with deep power fading observed on LOS microwave radio links in tropics
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The performance of line-of-sight microwave radio links in the tropics is critically dependent on the extreme variability of refraction effects of the intervening medium. The additional stability brought into the nocturnal boundary layer by the frequent occurrence of ground-based inversions coupled with the high humidity content of the tropical atmosphere produce anomalously larger refractivity gradients that persist for hours together and play havoc with the reliability of terrestrial line-of-sight microwave radio links, especially along the coastal paths and those other paths which are intercepted by river valleys. The fading patterns along with the associated physical mechanisms likely to be responsible for the observed nocturnal deep power fading in South-Eastern parts of India have been discussed along with the radio meteorological background of the region. The cumulative distribution statistics of received median signal level and its seasonal variability are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of optical propagation in a turbulent atmosphere using the split step method
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The split step method (SSM), initially formulated by Tappert and Hardin (1974) has been used by McCaskill and Ewart (1984) and Martin and Flatte (1988) to study plane wave propagation in random media. In the SSM, the role of the random medium is to introduce phase perturbation in each step of the algorithm from the transmitter to the receiver. The method is powerful because it can accommodate finite beam sources and an arbitrary refractive index power spectrum. The authors show the ability of the SSM to study plane wave and finite beam optical propagation in a two-dimensional turbulent atmosphere. The results from the modelling are compared with other numerical methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aperture distribution analysis of a flat plate antenna from short range pattern measurements
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Flat plate antennas have recently been developed which have square apertures with sides from 190 to 470 mm, operating between 11 and 12 GHz. Three examples are shown, an 8*8 circularly polarised (c.p.) array, a 16*16 c.p. array and a 20*20 dual linearly polarised array. The applications for these are DBS radio, DMAC DBS television, and Astra DBS television. These flat plate antennas have their distribution network and the antenna probes as an integrated structure, so that it is impractical to measure the distribution network in isolation. Accordingly a technique has been developed which deduces the performance of the distribution network form the observed radiation patterns. At the same time, the practical limitations set by anechoic chamber size can be calibrated out of the process. In the present case, measurements at a range of d/sup 2// lambda were involved (a 7 metre chamber).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The diagonalisation BFN for satellite reflector antennas with simultaneous overlapped multiple coverages
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author presents a synthesis method to determine the best electrical performance that can be achieved by an established array-fed reflector antenna configuration with a lossless BFN. By the hardware implementation of the mathematical diagonalisation technique, the network enabling the generation of any set of orthogonal output voltages with the minimum number of network components is found. During the synthesis process, the parameters of the diagonalisation BFN (DBFN), that exhibits one output port for each feed, are adjusted to explore the best achievable performance in terms of EOC directivity values. On the basis of these reference values, the method allows the definition of the optimum BFN, having a reduced number of output ports but still maintaining the DBFN architecture. The topology of this new network does not exhibit any crossing of the signal paths, thus becoming quite attractive. Comparisons between different synthesis techniques are also presented for a typical three coverage scenario.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The bi-polar planar near-field measurement and diagnostic facility
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Some of the unique features of a novel indoor bi-polar near-field measurement scanner, which has recently been completed at UCLA, are highlighted. Among the topics to be presented for the bi-polar near-field technique are: (a) bi-polar near-field concept, (b) mechanical implementation of a unique bi-polar scanner, (c) transformation techniques to the far field using various mathematical algorithms, (d) diagnostic and microwave holographic capabilities, (e) results of recent measurements, (f) inter-range measurement comparisons, etc. The bi-polar configuration consists of an antenna under test (AUT) mounted to a rotary positioner which rotates about one axis and a probe antenna mounted to a probe arm which rotates about a second axis. The bi-polar implementation results in planar near-field data collected on concentric rings with data samples located at the intersection with radial arcs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sir Edward Appleton: a centenary retrospect
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Sir Edward Appleton was the first person to discover the detailed structure of the ionosphere, and was awarded the Nobel Prize for this work. The salient features of his life are reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive multiple-beam array for wireless communications
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The wireless channel is characterized by multipaths with time-varying path losses, phase distortions (delays) and Doppler shifts. Adaptive multiple-beam forming with cochannel interference (CCI) is simulated using a ring array with periodic least mean square (LMS) training. The array performance in a multipath with CCI environment is evaluated in terms of symbol error rate (SER) using a QPSK signalling scheme. The SER degradation due to CCI depends on the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) and the CCI path DOA. Path tracking is also demonstrated for a single path moving in discrete steps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gabor series representation of scattered fields by dual reflector systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The principle of Gabor series representation is used to represent induced currents and reflector geometries in a confocal reflecting system. An efficient method to determine the scattered fields, based on an analytical development of the field integrals, is presented. The data localisation due to the Gabor representation and the stationary phase method, are combined in order to obtain the scattered field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of a dual-spiral printed antenna
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A dual-spiral antenna has the advantage that the two spiral elements are simultaneously fed from one source. The radiation characteristics of this antenna have been calculated using the current distribution. The calculations show that the dual spiral can radiate a circularly polarised wave. So far, the radiation efficiency of this antenna has not been described. Therefore, the authors reveal the radiation efficiency, together with the other radiation characteristics. The effects of the dielectric substrate thickness and dielectric constant (relative permittivity) on the radiation efficiency are presented and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determining the gravitational distortion of an antenna under test
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The paper serves to demonstrate the extremely close correlation of the gravitational distortion measured as a by-product of a series of RF range tests and the distortion predicted during the design stage by the standard engineering program, NASTRAN. The antenna under test (AUT) was a slotted waveguide array, 1.9*1.5 m built on a tubular steel space-frame. The 32 radiating waveguides were fed by a fixed 1:32 waveguide power divider, three sets of replaceable shims were used to provide three different beam shapes. Additionally, there were three different configurations of radiating waveguide used for the tests. Thus there were effectively nine AUTs; three waveguide sets each with three beams. In the test range, the pointing of the AUT in test range coordinates was measured by the range theodolite using four targets set at each corner of the antenna. Fine lines on the targets were set to be in a plane parallel to the best fit (least squares) plane through the radiating surface.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Randomization of the index of refraction in the tropospheric propagation
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: New formulations of the Maxwell equations in a heterogeneous medium are given. The author shows that the depolarization of an electromagnetic wave depends on the orthogonal projection of the gradients of the epsilon and mu constants on the E V-product H vector. The author shows that the colinearity of grade epsilon and grad mu requires that the electromagnetic wave is a locally plane wave. therefore with this condition fulfilled one is able to predict the propagation of an EM wave through the troposphere with knowledge of the gradient of the index of refraction. The author constructs a stochastic differential equation related to it and its reactualization uses the sampled data of this index in the troposphere. So one is able to predict the mean value and the covariance function of the amplitude phase and polarization of the received wave. The same method is applied to acoustical propagation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A millimetre wave semi-compact antenna test range
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A new technique for the measurement of antenna far-field patterns at millimetre wave frequencies is described and is based on a hybrid between the Compact Range and the near-field to far-field transformation method. A pillbox antenna forming the near-field probe performs instantaneous integration of the field in one dimension. Near-field patterns of antennas are measured and processed and far-field predictions produced within one minute on a standard 386 microcomputer. The technique is particularly suited for testing antennas on a production line. It is shown that far-field predictions from amplitude-only data can be obtained, hence providing a very low cost and yet accurate indoor antenna measurement facility. Modal filtering for reducing systematic noise in measured far-field patterns is demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Observations of the direction of arrival of HF signals propagated over high latitude and mid latitude paths
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Direction of arrival measurements have been made at two locations in Canada. One is a mid-latitude site observing an East-West path approximately tangential to the auroral oval. The other is a very high latitude site close to the geomagnetic pole at which signals propagating over two paths, one short path contained entirely within the polar cap and a second trans-auroral oval path on a similar true bearing were observed. Measurements at the mid-latitude site indicated that large bearing errors of up to about -90 degrees are observed during periods of enhanced geomagnetic activity. When large northerly bearing errors are observed at the mid-latitude site, large bearing errors are observed at the high latitude site for signals reflected from the polar cap ionosphere. A feature of these high latitude measurements is a large (+or-50 degrees ) quasi-periodic swing in the direction of arrival. These are attributed to reflection from patches of over-dense plasma.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Results of multiband (L,S,K/sub u/ band) propagation measurements for high elevation angle land mobile satellite channel
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors report on the results of a propagation campaign undertaken to characterize the fading nature of land mobile satellite channels at high elevation angles. The land mobile satellite channel behaviour may be summarized as follows: (1) as the path elevation angle to the satellite increases, the attenuation due to shadowing and multipath due to channel conditions reduce; (2) in general, signal attenuation increases as a function of increasing radio-frequency; (3) the effect of foliage density on the attenuation level has been found to be significant, particularly at higher elevation angles; and (4) the fading character of the land mobile satellite channel is significantly dependent upon the type of surrounding environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mechanical design of advanced shaped gridded reflectors for space applications
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: British Aerospace has over 20 years experience in the mechanical design and manufacture of advanced antenna reflectors for space applications and has to date, designed and manufactured over 90 such reflectors. The most significant being the low distortion C-band reflectors for INTELSAT VI and more recently the qualification of advanced shaped reflectors as part of an ESA study carried out by Fox et al. (1989). The detailed knowledge gained from these two programmes together with the company's wide experience in mechanical design/analysis of composite structures has enabled the development of advanced shaped gridded reflectors to meet the requirements of the ORION programme. The paper will describe the key aspects of the mechanical design that have been developed in order to realise this new type of reflector in addition to meeting the very stringent distortion and mass requirements. In addition the key development of an advanced new sunshield system and deployment trimming mechanisms are addressed. It concludes with a short hardware status summary.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of cavity backed aperture antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors apply the equivalence principle and the generalized network formulation to model the tangential electric field of multiple arbitrarily shaped apertures backed by a rectangular cavity, in terms of equivalent magnetic currents. The result is an integral equation for the unknown aperture current. This integral equation is then reduced to a matrix equation using the method of moments. The method is used to investigate the characteristics of these aperture antennas in particular the end-loaded, and H-antennas are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of rotationally symmetric broad-band monopoles over circular ground plane
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The two analysis methods compared are the method of moments (MM) with surface currents and the method of moments combined with the geometrical theory of diffraction (MM+GTD). The author investigates the condition number of the MM matrix and on the basis of this calculation the basis function chosen has smaller extent near to the coaxial excitation and the expansion functions are weighted with the distance from the excitation point. Using this method the stability can be held even at ground planes with greater radius. The results of MM and MM+GTD are in good agreement when the radius of the ground plane is greater than 2.4 wavelengths depending on the resonance frequency of the monopole but the computational time of MM is considerably greater when the radius of ground plane is greater than a wavelength.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of propagation effects on 40 GHz short haul radio systems using experimental based estimation of rain structure
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors describe an experimental data-base which contains propagation parameters at 30 GHz, the inversion technique used to assess parameters of rain structure and the estimated fade statistics at working frequencies. The data-base contains the channel characterization of a 5.5 km terrestrial radio link located in Rome, and contains about 300 events covering less than three years. The aim of the experiment was the determination of attenuation and depolarisation due to rain. The performances of a proposed SDH-compatible broadband local radio system, operating at 37-39.5 GHz, are evaluated using these data and a comparison with the results obtained using CCIR prediction method is performed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling the effectiveness of RAM coatings on PEC scatterers in the resonance region
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The use of radar absorbing materials (RAMs) on the surface of PEC scatterers to reduce their radar cross section or to suppress coupling to local objects, is receiving growing interest. To model their effectiveness numerical techniques are required to solve the associated electromagnetic equations. The difficulties associated with modelling such problems, particularly when the structure has dimensions in the resonance region were discussed by Medgyesi-Mitschang and Wang (1989) and are associated with the inhomogeneities of the scatterer and the concentration of the electromagnetic fields in the layer of RAM.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sector coverage antennas for broadcast applications in the millimetre wave region
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Transmit antenna designs for radio systems used for video distribution applications in the millimetre wave region have been established which give optimum coverage areas and make efficient use of the available spectrum. A specific design of wide beamwidth sector coverage antenna have been identified which provides a circular coverage area with the transmitter sited on the periphery of the area for the frequency bands from 28 to 60 GHz. Examples of transmit horn antennas used to provide circular coverage areas for video distribution applications are described. Further applications could occur in the 40.5 to 42.5 GHz band which has been allocated by the Radiocommunications Agency of the DTI for multichannel TV broadcasting as a supplement to cable systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 90 degrees offset parabolic reflector antennas at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Describes the method used to design a series of single 90 degrees offset parabolic reflector antennas with a conical corrugated feed horn at 14, 9 and 3 mm wavelengths. The radiation patterns and the phase center are calculated by Gaussian beam mode analysis. The antenna pattern and beam efficiency are calculated by the aperture field method. The experimental data are shown. These antennas were used in microwave and millimeter wave radiometers; demonstrating their mechanical and electrical performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical modelling of cavity backed apertures using transmission-line modelling (TLM)
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Transmission-line modelling (TLM) is used to simulate the effects of apertures on the internal behaviour of a resonant cavity. TLM is free from the limitations imposed on some other methods of analysis and is thus a generally applicable analysis and design tool. The main strengths of TLM in this class of applications are noted and comparisons are presented with experimental results to validate this approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison among prediction methods of site diversity system performances
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Site diversity is a useful countermeasure to overcome severe rain attenuation in satellite communication links. several prediction models of the diversity gain. The authors have tested seven different prediction models of site diversity gain against the results of 47 experiments with various geometrical/radioelectrical system characteristics, at different frequencies from 11 to 30 GHz. Four models have been classified as empirical, the other three as physical models. The average, RMS, and sigma of the difference between the estimated and measured percent gain show that the empirical Hodge's model (see Radio Sci., vol.17, no.6, p.1393-9, 1982). (which was obtained by a best fit over 22 of the 47 experiments here used) behaves better than the others giving the lowest value of sigma and a small average underestimate. Nevertheless, two physical models-those of Matricciani's and Capsoni et al. (see Eur. Trans. Telecom. Relat. Technol., vol.2, no.6, 715-27, 1991; and Radio Sci., vol.22, no.3, p.387-93, 1987, respectively)-which are intrinsically more powerful as they can be also used to predict other propagation quantities, show results very similar to those of Hodge's that confirm their wide range of applicability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ASYRIO: a reconfigurable antenna for a second generation of the Spanish satellite (HISPASAT-II)
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Project ASYRIO (antenna system reconfigurable in orbit) studies the technological development of variable components over a real scenario, the Spanish satellite, to establish realistic BFN requirements. The electrical design requires a powerful software which takes into account the complex coverages from the two satellite locations and allows for a simultaneous optimization of the reflector dimensions and cluster geometry. The authors present the electrical design of the FSS HISPASAT antenna as well as the software used for the design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 12-element printed array antenna for INMARSAT-M maritime communications
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In the maritime satellite communication system, the mechanism of 3 or 4-axis antenna mount is usually introduced rather than that of 2-axis antenna mount despite its simple mechanism. Because in the mechanism of the 2-axis antenna mount, as the antenna points toward high elevation angle, particularly in zenith direction, the tracking system become uncontrollable. The disadvantage is overcome by introducing electrical steering into the 2-axis antenna mount. From these points of view, the authors have developed an electrically steered high efficiency 12-element printed array antenna composed of a spiral antenna with a reflector.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved analysis of the conical horn to free space junction
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Previously in the analysis of feedhorns with the modal-matching technique (MMT), a further method such as the aperture field method or spherical wave expansion was needed in order to describe the radiated fields. In the theory presented by the authors, the MMT is used to evaluate all fields. The application of the MMT to infinite extended areas permits the inclusion of the transition from feedhorn to free space in the analysis. Furthermore, a coordinate transformation with the help of a Zwischenmedium intermediate medium is discussed, which is needed, if the fields inside the feedhorn are analysed with the MMT in cylindrical coordinates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Azimuthal distribution of noise and interface at HF
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The predictions of atmospheric and man-made noise in CCIR Reports 322 and 258 are for short lossless, grounded, single vertical monopole antennas, but practical antennas may differ from the CCIR reference antenna in many respects. The antenna directivity may be expected to affect both noise and spectral occupancy statistics. Experimental information on the effects of directivity on noise is scarce, and in some respects conflicting. Most previous spectrum occupancy studies have used omnidirectional antennas, but some results with directional antennas have recently been reported. The paper reports further measurements at a site in Southern England.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the implementation of global interpolating functions for shaped reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The synthesis of microwave reflector antennas yields numerically defined surfaces which must be interpolated in order to permit the evaluation of the radiation field and its check against designer specifications, which usually requires a considerable computational effort. Aiming at the optimization of this process, the implementation of two global interpolating functions-quintic pseudo-splines (QPS) and polynomial Fourier series (PFS)-was explored towards its application to the synthesis of a highly shaped reflector antenna for use in nodal stations. The versatility and greater stability of the former was then ascertained. New aspects of their applicability to the synthesis and analysis of reflector antennas based on extended numerical tests, including dual shaped offset systems, are reported. Also, the application of a third interpolating function, the Jacobi polynomial sinusoidal expansion (JPSE), to the global representation of numerically defined reflectors is investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical representation for finite arrays of rectangular waveguide apertures
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A simple numerical representation for arrays of different-sized rectangular waveguide apertures has been described. The analytical expression of mutual admittance given by T.S. Bird (see IEEE Trans. Antennas Propag., vol.38, no.2, 166-72 1990) is evaluated by means of a direct integration method where the highly oscillatory integrand is locally approximated by a linear form and solved in closed form to evaluate the contribution of a single incremental area. Expressions of all applicable symmetry and reciprocity conditions have been derived. The need for using a large number of modes has also been observed. The effectiveness of the theory in predicting the performance of rectangular waveguide arrays, with closely packed elements, has been analyzed comparing measured and computed data of two different arrays. Though the numerical results denote a substantial improvement of the array modelling, the need of more accurate coupling formulas, together with the study of the scattering matrix of the horns, have to be further investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer modelling of antennas:A comparison of available techniques
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author surveys the computer methods available for the analysis and synthesis of antennas and their associated components and to providing some guidance in the applications and limitations of the various available methods. The methods discussed are volume element methods (FDTD, TLM, FEA, mode matching), surface element methods (method of moments PO), ray methods (GTD and GO), and hybrid methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of radiation patterns for HF mobile communications using the method of characteristic modes
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Mobile antenna systems have always presented engineers with a challenge. One particular problematic situation is when the antenna and structure on which it is mounted are comparable in size. Here induced current on the structure may dramatically alter the antenna characteristics. Much effort has therefore been applied, using the method of moments, in the development of modelling techniques for accurate analysis of the problem. An alternative approach is presented using the method of characteristic modes (CM). The technique allows a set of orthogonal functions to be defined from the moment method impedance matrix data to represent the current flow. This permits the antenna and associated structure to be considered as one. Pattern synthesis may hence be achieved by optimizing the modes of the total structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of multi-step amplitude quantized weights for solid-state planar phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A new method is presented which applies the multi-step amplitude quantization method to control the sidelobe level of a planar rectangular array antenna. The different sidelobe level requirement in azimuthal and elevational planes are achieved. In other areas, the sidelobe level can also be controlled. This method take the advantage of that proposed by Zheng and Guo (1991), Guo and Xue (1986, 1989) and Xue (see Proc. of EM science conf., p.231, 1992). The amplitude distribution is chosen according to probability theory. In the determination of the amplitude steps, the optimizing method is used to minimize the pattern variance and the calculation of simultaneous integrated equations is avoided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Green's function analysis of microstrip antennas using Chebyshev decomposition
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The spectral domain technique, expressed as Fourier-Bessel (Hankel) or Sommerfeld integrals (SI), is used to set up a dynamical model for the microstrip. The SI are solved via an efficient algorithm based on decomposing part of the integrand in Chebyshev polynomials. The method is particularly well suited to solve the electric field integral equation for the surface current. Comparison with published results are made which proves the validity of the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparative study of two different formulations of coupled mode theory for analysing rectangular dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The differences between two distinct formulations of the coupled mode method are analyzed and justified. The difference is interpreted in terms of the continuity of the axial components of the electromagnetic field. The original Schelkunoff formulation (1952) of the coupled mode method is shown to converge in a more efficient way than Ogusu's formulation (1977).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Retrieval of the atmospheric ozone profiles from microwave measurements at 2.7 mm
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The necessity of accurate monitoring of the ozone concentration on a global scale is caused by increased ozone destruction in the stratosphere. Ozone concentration may be measured from the ground, balloon, aircraft or satellite by microwave spectrometers operating at the 101, 110, 142 or 206 GHz ozone lines. An original portable spectrometer operating at 2.7 mm (110 GHz line) is used at the Central Aerological Observatory for profiling the stratospheric ozone. In the processing of ground-based measurements a difficult problem is to account for the tropospheric absorption caused by oxygen and water vapour. It is well known that the vertical distribution of oxygen is sufficiently stable in contrast with the changeable content of the water vapour in the atmosphere. The flight of a high-altitude balloon with a spectrometer on board allows one to carry out microwave measurements above the top of the troposphere. The contribution of the tropospheric absorption may be evaluated from comparison of these data with simultaneous ground-based measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Large finite array analysis
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors discuss a study to develop and test methods of fully predicting large antenna array performance using infinite array data. The methods devised are presented below, together with comparisons of predicted finite array performance and measured data from a 163 element waveguide 16 array. The routes presented from infinite to finite array data produce good results. The direct Fourier windowing technique from infinite to finite array patterns is quickest and produces reasonable results for any type of array element. The more rigorous methods that deduce the actual array couplings produce more accurate results for simple single mode element types. Information such as individual element active reflection coefficients for arbitrary scan angles is easy to deduce.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method for measuring the scattering pattern of a building on VHF TV broadcasting waves
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors propose a method for quickly and effectively measuring the scattering pattern of a building on TV broadcasting waves in the VHF band. The scattering pattern obtained from this method takes into account all the complex properties of the building materials. This method utilizes the concept of determining the scattering pattern of an object from a knowledge of the near-field distribution using the Huygen's principles. The scattering field distribution on the surface of the wall is measured and then the scattering pattern is calculated by using it. A probe antenna developing the scattering field is necessary for this method. The authors describe the radiation characteristics of the probe antenna, and an experimental result which was carried out on their campus using the video carrier wave of VHF TV broadcasting (frequency 205.25MHz, TM incidence) is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Statistical behaviour of refractivity gradient in the tropics
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The knowledge of the spatial behaviour of the refractivity in the lower troposphere is an essential information for the design of UHF and SHF radio links, as well as for the evaluation of interference between terrestrial communication systems. The paper presents results of refractivity measurements at 16 sites in several climatic regions in Brazil. An experiment underway in seven additional links, aiming to estimate the effective K factor of the Earth from attenuation measurements in diffracted links is also described. Depending on the site, different measurement methods were employed: radio sonde measurements or direct measurements using refractometers. The probability distributions obtained from measured data indicate that, in tropical regions, the media values of refractivity gradient are usually significantly higher than those found in temperate climates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of the radiation from finite-size one-dimensional leaky-wave antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors study the different types of wave components that comprise the total aperture field of a planar leaky-wave antenna, and show how each influences the radiation pattern. The two main components of the aperture field are the radiation (continuous-spectrum) field and the surface-wave field. The radiation field is further decomposed into the ,leaky-wave field and the space-wave field. The authors also study how a finite-size aperture affects the radiation from the different aperture field components, and thus influences the total radiation pattern. The effects of scan angle, in particular, on the radiation from the different aperture field components is investigated. The authors also study the accuracy of two different simple formulas for determining the finite-aperture radiation pattern, one based solely on the radiated pattern of the leaky wave, and the other using an improved formulation called the subtraction method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Phased array antenna with microstrip sub-arrays: a solution to reduce the number of phase shifters
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The design of an array of printed antennas for use in a weather forecasting radar system is presented. The results described relate only to the array geometry and phase commands, with the purpose of reducing the number of phase shifters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modified magnetic field formulation for aperture antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A novel integral boundary formulation, for determining the surface current density, the near and far-zone fields due to arbitrarily shaped conducting bodies in the presence of a known primary source is used to solve problems related to aperture antennas. A surface electric charge density is used as another equivalent source, in addition to the usual fictitious electric current density, so that a Modified Magnetic Field Integral Equation (MMFIE) can be derived to simulate the field outside the body. This approach allows the expansion of both unknown sources by means of two sets of subdomain-type pulse functions without causing inconsistencies or anomalies in the solution obtained by the method of moments (MM). Results for a cube show the validity of the MMFIE; examples of applications to rectangular truncated waveguides and flanged waveguide/coax adapters are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of wind on sea surface from polarimetric scattering
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A classical method used to obtain the RCS of the sea surface is the small perturbation model. This method is extended to the vectorial case, to obtain the polarimetric signature of the ocean surface, from a classical two-scale surface for sea surface model. An expression of this signature is first given by the sea surface Mueller matrix. The study of the terms of the averaged Mueller matrix shows that the number of coefficients can be reduced to a vector whose dimension is minimal (five). From this defined reduced vector, a Bayes estimator is built (maximum likelihood ratio test), enabling the direction and speed of the wind to be estimated, from an averaging of measurements of the polarimetric sea surface backscattering. A second formalization of the sea surface backscattering signature is proposed, which consists of a backscattering model for a single instantaneous measurement. For this purpose, the instantaneous signature of the sea surface is formalized by a 'polarization fork', which is described by the five Euler parameters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of frequency selective surfaces with open and short circuited elements
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Dyadic Green's function methodology is used to analyze periodic structures with open or short circuited square rings as elements. The possibility of using this geometry for multiband operation is investigated, and the variation of its reflectivity with the incident angle of the illuminating plane wave is studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real bivector representation of target backscattering matrix and the Mueller matrix construction
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Vector decomposition of the coherent backscattering matrix conveniently leads to generalisation to partially coherent scattering via the Hermitian covariance matrix. Recently, it was shown how this formalism could be incorporated within the Stokes-Mueller calculus, but the requirement for complex vectors and covariance matrices leads to some problems in defining transformation laws. These are overcome by obtaining a closely related real representation of the coherent scattering matrix as a four-dimensional bivector. This permits a description of coherent scattering within an extended Stokes algebra, and a particularly simple construction of the Mueller matrix in terms of the bivector.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direction of arrival measurements of oblique chirp sounder signals at a high latitude site
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The performance of high frequency direction finding systems is known to be related to the mode content of the incoming signal and to the frequency of operation. Furthermore, HF propagation via the high latitude ionosphere is often disturbed with, for example, the signal arriving at the receiver over paths well displaced from the great circle. Observations at Alert, located high in the Canadian Arctic, indicate that large off great circle bearings on fixed frequency signals are associated with well defined features on oblique ionograms taken over the paths of interest. In order to investigate further these phenomena, a system has been developed which can measure the bearings of signals radiated by the worldwide network of BR chirp sounder transmitters across the full range of propagating frequencies. Preliminary tests of the system were undertaken in Ottawa during August 1991 and at Cheltenham during January 1992 with further measurements at Alert during April 1992.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improvements in the design of reconfigurable reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Three schemes are described which reduce or compensate for the effects of pillowing in reconfigurable mesh reflector antennas. A multiple attachment scheme is described and shown to be effective. In another method large buttons are used and the level of pillowing maintained with far fewer actuators. Finally a method of dielectric compensation is outlined which would be especially suitable for a retrofit. Among these the multiple attachment method is the most promising but would require elastic strings in practice. This runs counter to the proposed use of rigid member linkages used to reduce the number of actuators but it is similar to schemes used in deployable reflectors. The use of large buttons shows clear benefit and should be adopted in any future design using buttons to control the shape of a mesh. Finally dielectric compensation is effective but it adds to the antenna mass.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EM coupling computation of a portable communication dipole-antenna proximate to the abdomen of an operator man model
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: EM coupling effects of an operator man body on a portable communication dipole-antenna located proximate to the abdomen surface (the distance is less than 1 cm) was studied. Coupled integral equations (CIE) and the moment method (MoM) were used to numerically compute the EM interaction between the human body and the radiating dipole antenna. Antenna characteristics, e.g., input impedance, current distribution, radiation efficiency, and antenna patterns, coupled with the present body, are determined. EM energy deposition into the body and the body-absorbed power are also calculated. Numerical examples at the 840-MHz portable communication frequency band are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A decade bandwidth electronically tunable microwave phase changer
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Describes a novel electronically tunable phase changer which is usable over a decade of bandwidth and is based on a distributed amplifier used in reverse gain mode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of personal communication handset antennas in their operating environment
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Personal communication handsets are used in either outdoor or indoor propagation conditions, and usually in close proximity to the user's head and hand. The specification and design of antennas for handsets requires a knowledge of the effects of the operating environment on the antenna and system performance. The user' s head and hand will affect the radiation pattern of the antenna, but the effect on the link performance will also be a function of the propagation conditions. The angular spread of the signals received by the handset will vary with the environment, so that the effective gain of the handset antenna is a function of this angular spread and the radiation pattern. Statistical measures are needed to describe performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reflection and transmission of the radiowaves in regular ionosphere taking into account wave phenomena
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors suggest a new method of calculation of the matrix of complex reflection and transparency coefficients for an arbitrary ionospheric layer, either magnetized or isotropic. The main advantage of this approach compared with other methods is connected with taking into consideration the overbarrier reflection and tunnel-effect. The profile of electron concentration and effective collision frequency can be arbitrary, and the layer thickness can reach more than millions of wavelengths. If the reflection and transparency coefficients are calculated over sufficiently wide frequency ranges one can calculate the distortions of signals reflected by the ionosphere and the radiowave fields using Fourier transformation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reflector antennas for high power, near field elliptical spot beams with circular polarisation
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A set of three reflectors using elliptical surfaces to provide near field focusing, each having a cluster of circularly polarised feeds providing multi-band performance has been developed. Frequency bandwidth at any one band is typically 10%. The antenna configuration was dictated heavily by system needs for bandwidth, spot size and overall efficiency. Spot size and shape were set after a trade- off including achievable power density, spot vertical and horizontal dimensions, spot alignment under worst case environmental conditions, etc. In order to minimise cost, the design was taken directly from computer model to hardware. Reflectors were analysed using physical optics and GTD, feeds were designed using mode matching techniques with finite element analysis used for certain feed components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Embedded ionospheric sounding systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors detail some of the research and concepts that have been developed within the Hull-Lancaster Communications Research Group at the University of Hull aimed at providing an embedded ionospheric sounding capability that would exist as a normal function of an adaptive radio terminal. In particular, close attention has been paid to designing sounders for long-range HF radio systems that can operate in a beyond line-of-sight mode. Sounders developed include a segmented swept FM and complementary sequence sounder for HF radio propagation analysis and that can be used by an adaptive frequency management system. All the sounders developed are heavily dependent upon the use of powerful high-speed digital signal processing (DSP) devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interference mechanisms which affect frequency reuse on short line-of-sight millimetric links
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: At microwave frequencies, clear-air refraction (at small time percentages) and troposcatter (at large time percentages) are generally assumed to be the dominant propagation mechanisms for the coordination of line-of-sight systems; this is due to the long paths (>30 km) and large separations between adjacent paths (typically hundreds of kilometres). For shorter path separations over land, terrain diffraction must also be considered. The authors discuss the importance of the various interference mechanisms. In particular non-great circle mechanisms (such as building scatter) are shown to be important. These mechanisms are not adequately covered by current prediction methods. The models are discussed. An experimental programme of building, terrain and rain scatter measurements at 38 GHz has been planned to test the models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quarter-wavelength microstrip antenna for the handset of DECT system
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The viability of a lambda /4 microstrip patch as the antenna of the DECT handset is analyzed. The simple transmission line and cavity models are used to analyze the antenna and to design the prototypes. The input impedance, bandwidth and radiation patterns are obtained theoretically and experimentally for several prototypes, and they satisfy the requirements of the DECT system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of aperture-coupled patch antennas for CAD applications
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A formulation is suggested in order to calculate the scattering matrix of the two port antenna module with a more CAD oriented approach. Correspondingly, a simple equivalent network is obtained, which is useful in the synthesis processes. Some lumped element of the equivalent network are evaluated by typical full-wave reaction integrals, making use of some simplifying assumptions for the current distributions on the slot and the microstrip-line. Furthermore, in order to describe the storage of the reactive energy near the coupling slot toward the patch, a parallel plate waveguide model is used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Finite element/moment method analysis of waveguide coupling by means of apertures or slots
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An equivalence principle is invoked to divide the problem into three separate regions which are then coupled by enforcing the continuity of magnetic fields at the interfaces of these regions. A coupled set of equations are derived by invoking appropriate boundary conditions, dyadic Green's functions and variational approaches, to find the tangential electric field on the upper and the lower surfaces of the aperture or slot. A finite element method is adopted to discretize the aperture or slot region. In order to overcome the singularity at conducting corners and edges, edge-based expansion functions are chosen. The predominant advantage of this approach is that it is no longer necessary to know the dyadic Green's functions in the aperture region. Hence the technique can be employed to analyse waveguide coupling problems involving complex slots or apertures. The method has been successfully applied to the coupling problem comprising two identical waveguides containing a slot in the common broadwall. Comparisons between the results obtained from this method and those from a moment method are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new polarization calibration technique for a large phased array with maximum baseline approximately=220 Km
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Long-baseline interferometric arrays are used in radioastronomy to produce polarisation images of the fine structure of radio sources allowing the study of their nature. The multi-element radio-linked interferometer network (MERLIN) is an array of six 25 m dishes connected by microwave links with maximum telescope separation of 217 km, recording both left and right hand circular polarisation (LCP, RCP) at approximately=128 Mbits/second in real-time. Accurate calibration is difficult because of phase-instabilities of the incoming wavefront caused by ionospheric and tropospheric effects. In addition, crosstalk between LCP and RCP channels in the MERLIN receivers corrupts the signals and is equivalent to an elliptical feed response. The aim of the calibration process is to reconstruct the LCP and RCP phase and amplitude information and to solve for feed crosstalk which can be corrected in off-line data processing. The standard strategy is to derive corrections from observations of different radio sources with known polarisation characteristics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Teaching program for microwave antenna theory
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author presents a computer program which was developed at the Department of Microwave Telecommunication of the University of Budapest to introduce and educate students in microwave antennas. The program has already been used for undergraduate and graduate level students. Using the program the theory of antennas can he attained faster and it is very easy to demonstrate the effects of the antenna parameters on the antenna properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electromagnetic design of high performance frequency-selective large sandwich radome
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: System performance requirements place increasing demands on radome design. Specifications on ground based radomes become much tighter as a direct consequence of rapid growth and development of advanced techniques for radar and communication systems. Low sidelobe, multi-frequency and wider bandwidth antenna systems are of particular interest. These impose on radomes an increasing demand for high transmission and lower boresight shift, cross polarization, sidelobe degradation and reflection. In the design of large sandwich radomes, scattering effects from the seams play a significant role. To obtain a high performance radome, one should consider both reducing the scattering from the individual seams and optimizing the seam geometry.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Propagation of radio waves in underground tunnels and underground radio systems
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A typical potash mine consists of a network of interconnected straight tunnels with rectangular cross section located about 3000 feet underground. The tunnel system may be over 10 kilometers in length. A wireless system is needed to distribute video information, radio telephony and digital control information within the tunnel network. A program was initiated to obtain the propagation data which is needed to optimize system design. An experimental system named 'distributed antenna system' (DAS) was designed and installed in the Central Canada Potash facility. The DAS makes use of the unique propagation characteristics of the potash tunnel network and can be used in place of the more expensive leaky feeder system used in other mines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new model for two dimensional light modulated microwave imaging array
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A new model for a two dimensional laser beam scanned microwave imaging array is described. The array element is multiloaded segmented dipole, which could be a dipole with photosensitive elements between the segments. Theoretical studies show that the current along the dipole can be reduced to a very small value, giving very high modulation and low mutual coupling. Experimental results are presented at 8.4 GHz with an ordinary dipole and a physical model of the segmented dipole. The results agree very well with theoretical case and the effective modulation factor is about 92%. This type of array can be used for general field imaging, the exact details depending on the system requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved integral formulation for conducting bodies of revolution
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Presents an improved procedure, by using both surface and interior integral equations for conducting bodies of revolution, in which certain field components, such as the tangential E-field, vanish not only on the radiating surface, but also in the interior of the radiator, therefore the deficiencies of the previous procedure in the vicinity of the interior resonant frequencies can be overcome. A general computer program is written, and sample computations are given for a sphere. It is shown that a unique solution can be obtained using the improved method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direction of arrival of radio signals within buildings
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Within buildings the spread in the time of arrival of UHF radio signals depends on reflection and scattering from the structure of the buildings. To demonstrate this process the authors have carried out measurements of the direction of arrival, DOA, of signals using a synthetic aperture array antenna. Measurements were made at a frequency of 870 MHz. Propagation processes such as penetration through walls and floors, reflection, scattering and diffraction by the steel frame of the building, the beams and the columns have been identified and demonstrated by the measurement results. The waveguide effect of the corridors in guiding the signals to the receiver has also been demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dual-frequency receiving antennas for the Nobeyama radioheliograph using frequency selective subreflectors
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: It is quite important in radio astronomy to observe at several frequency bands for investigation on characteristics of radio emission. Especially in observing solar radio flares, which suddenly occur and rapidly change in intensity and structure, simultaneous observations are necessary at multiple frequencies to determine spectra of the sources. In order to observe solar flares at short centimeter wavelengths, the authors have developed a dual-frequency receiving antennas for the Nobeyama radioheliograph using frequency selective subreflectors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ENLACE-analysis and prediction of rainfall rate and rain attenuation distributions
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The ENLACE software was developed to analyse and characterise rain rate distributions and to calculate rain attenuation distributions in line-of-sight and satellite links using several different prediction methods. The program can be used to fit analytical functions, such as log-normal, gamma, log-power and Moupfouma's distributions, to measured rain rate distributions. The measured distribution and its analytical approximations, can be compared with those of the CCIR rain climates. Rain attenuation prediction can be performed using either measured rain rate data, fitted analytical distributions or CCIR climate distributions. Ten methods for rain attenuation prediction proposed, are implemented, including the current CCIR method. Routines for calculation of prediction errors are also available. The software, runs on IBM-PC compatible computers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: GTD pattern analysis of antennas on a finite ground plane by using modified edge representation
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A method of modified edge representation (MER) for flat plates are applied for the pattern analysis of GPS patch antennas mounted on a rectangular ground plane. In the MER, the contribution of FW-EECs (equivalent currents) to total EECs are weighted by the function of the angle between the modified edge and the real edge. The key feature of this approach is that uniform fields are predicted everywhere though only classical diffraction coefficients are used in first-order diffraction. The secondary diffraction is included as well. The ray-tracing is greatly simplified by introducing other fictitious edges for MER. Numerical results for diffraction from the GPS patch antenna mounted on a flat plates demonstrate the potential of MER.
