The EECs derived are specially refined to MER; the physical meaning of the MER and the weighting of FW-EECs should be validated theoretically in future study.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Indoor propagation measurements application to mobile channel modelling
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors present and discuss results of a measurement campaign, carried out in order to investigate penetration losses into buildings and indoor attenuation contributions due to floors and ceilings. More generally, outdoor-indoor propagation characteristics, using low base station antennas are investigated, at 900 and 1700 MHz, with the goal of providing data to be further used for modelling purposes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Satellite radiotomography of the global ionosphere structure and irregularities
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors suggest a method of phase-difference radiotomography (RT) based on measurements of the Doppler frequency of a radiowave from a satellite. The reconstruction of the 2D distribution of the electron density then becomes a problem of RT using phase-difference measurements. Using the piece-plane approximation based on triangular elements, and an approximation of higher orders the difference system is transformed to the large sparse system of linear equations. An experimental complex using a probing source onboard the navigation satellite was built.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Space diversity and fade duration statistics for two over-water, line-of-sight, C-band links in the mid-Atlantic coast of the United States
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors characterize space diversity, and fade duration statistics associated with two over-water, line-of-sight, C-Band links in the Mid-Atlantic coast of the United States over the year period 1 June 1989-31 May 1990. This information is important in that it establishes the potential for fade margin reduction in a system employing space or route diversity methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resonance characteristics of longitudinal shunt slots in a planar slotted-waveguide antenna
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Shows how an entire domain moment method can be employed to accurately investigate the effect of both internal and external mutual coupling on the resonant properties of slots in a planar slotted-waveguide antenna. The analysis is initiated by establishing a set of integral equations. Instead of assuming the field distribution on the slots, a set of basis functions are employed to simulate precisely the field. Galerkin's method is applied to transform the integral equations into a matrix equation. Resonant length and resonant conductance are computed in the presence of both internal and external mutual coupling. The results are in good agreement with experimental measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling parasitically-coupled patch antennas using the finite-difference time-domain technique
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: With the increasing interest in the use of printed circuit techniques for the manufacture of millimetre-wave antennas, there is a need to accurately model the radiation, coupling, susceptive loading and resonance mechanisms in order to determine the antennas' input and far-field responses. For instance, with antenna elements fabricated on a high permittivity dielectric, such as alumina, the resonant behaviour of the antenna may be strongly dependent upon the size of the dielectric owing to the level of surface wave radiation. Furthermore, printed antennas tend to be formed into arrays of elements, and therefore coupling and feed line effects must also be considered in the design procedure. The aim of the paper is to demonstrate the use of a general field solving technique in the analysis of patch antennas. In this example, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique is applied to determine the characteristics of a mutually-coupled array of narrow microstrip patches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A linear and planar array simulation program for a Macintosh personal computer
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The aim in writing this piece of software was to provide an array designer, or student studying antenna theory, with an interactive tool to aid in visualising the effects of the numerous parameters that specify a planar array. This work combines a variety of methods to calculate results for several physical situations. A novel representation of errors in element placement and excitation has also been developed, allowing their effect on radiation pattern to be assessed on the basis of a number of Monte-Carlo trials. Furthermore, the modular program structure, and the use of a series of menus and windows for data input, ensure easy expansion of the software in the future. The basis of the program is the 'model file', which contains the complete definition of the antenna in terms of the element type, the array geometry, the element excitations and any tolerances to he applied to the excitation parameters during plotting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Basic measurements which relate to the propagation of millimetre waves through finely dispersed materials
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author describes a measurement procedure for studies of propagation of millimetre-waves over short ranges and though dispersed materials. The procedure uses high density distributions of particles in an open resonator system in such a way that effects basic to scattering and propagation may be studied in relation to closely observed particle shapes and distributions. Specific areas where the laboratory measurement could provide a useful contribution are: (1) prediction of the attenuation created by particles of material of any known dielectric constant; (2) studies of the effect of particles of mixed composition, particularly where one constituent is water; and (3) studies of the effect of nonuniform and time varying distribution densities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of measured scattering data in modelling and predicting the attenuation characteristics of hail and graupel at 10 GHz 34 GHz and 70 GHz
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: One approach to providing information on the interaction of electromagnetic waves with such particles is to fabricate individual particles in the laboratory and to measure the interactions while observing closely the particle's shape and physical condition. The authors describe an extensive study of simulated single hailstones and graupel which has recently been completed where scattering measurements (of extinction or total loss cross-sections) were made in open resonators at 10 GHz, 34 GHz and 70 GHz. The principal aims of this work are firstly, to measure the extinction cross-sections of the range of particle types and conditions and to relate these results to modelled results for single particles, and secondly, to investigate the possibilities and shortcomings of using the results in combination with known distributions of size of naturally occurring hail to estimate the attenuations (dB/km) likely to be encountered by propagating waves.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: UTD analysis of the hyperbolic cylinders for applications to onboard aircraft antennas
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The ray solution for the hyperbolic cylinder is yet to be derived. The authors present a systematic derivation of the ray-geometric parameters on a canonical hyperbolic cylinder for the UTD antenna analysis. Such an analysis is of interest in determining the optimal locations for the onboard aircraft antennas required in the telecommunications applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Satellite communication channel long term fade characteristics at 20 GHz
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors describe the equipment used in experiments using the Olympus and MAYAK satellites. An initial analysis of data obtained over a few months of the one year duration of the experiment is presented. Typical fade rates were <or=1.3 dB/sec.<<ETX>>

articleTitle: An experiment for propagation studies at 94 GHz
publicationTitle: 1993 Eighth International Conference on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The experiment presented was conceived to study bistatic scattering as well as attenuation on a short horizontal path. The characteristics of the rain (rain rate and drop size) are measured simultaneously with the transmitted electromagnetic power for various scattering angles. This allows one to compute a theoretical received power for each rain event and to compare it with the experimental result. One can also study the influence of the drop size repartition.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
